newsitem.title: CHILE: GasAndes pipeline hit by 2nd court order - report.
newsitem.headline: GasAndes pipeline hit by 2nd court order - report.

text.p: A Chilean court has granted a second injunction against the GasAndes pipeline project after fresh complaints that builders have not finished safety measures at the scheme, reported newspaper El Mercurio Wednesday.
The order, the second against the project this month, has killed hopes that the pipeline will be able to begin pumping natural gas from Argentina Thursday as planned, it said.
GasAndes officials declined to comment on the report but a spokesman said the group would issue a statement later Wednesday.
The pipeline is being built by a consortium owned by Chilean power generator Chilgener and Canadian energy company NOVA Corp.

The ruling by a court in the town of San Miguel followed complaints that GasAndes has not finished building a dam near a farm as agreed under a deal with the land's owners giving a right-of-way over the property.
GasAndes plans to open the pipeline officially August 7 in a ceremony attended by Chilean President Eduardo Frei and Argentine President Carlos Menem.

The pipeline will pump natural gas to Santiago across the Andes from Mendoza in central Argentina. It will use an existing pipeline to bring the gas to Mendoza from gas fields in the province of Neuquen.
